dev.err.action_failed.note: Error reply the apps show when a request to the device failed with an error the device can't translate (a database's or the operating system's own words). Shown only in languages other than English: an English request gets the error alone, as it always did. {detail} is that error, in English.

dev.err.demo.text: This is a demo device: changes are turned off.
dev.err.demo.note: Error reply on a public demo device (a device anyone can sign in to with a published password, to try Off The Cloud) to anything that would change it: uploading, deleting, renaming, settings, the password, sharing. The apps show it when the person tries.

dev.err.error_detail.note: Error reply the device sends when signing in failed, or when a friend's device asked something about a friendship and it failed. {detail} is the reason: one of the device's own sentences, or an error in English it can't translate.

dev.err.internal.note: Error reply the apps show when the device hit an unexpected fault while answering a request (a bug on the device). Nothing the user can do about it but try again.

dev.err.not_authenticated.note: Error reply to a request that needs the owner signed in (or a friend's device authenticated) on a connection that isn't: the session is gone, for example because the device restarted. The apps go back to the sign-in screen.

dev.err.not_in_container.text: Not available in Docker: the server the device runs on looks after its disks and network.
dev.err.not_in_container.note: Error reply on a device that runs in Docker (a container on a home server or NAS) to setting up its disks or joining a wireless network, which the first-run setup and older apps may ask for: the server the container runs on looks after both.

dev.err.not_on_this_instance.note: Error reply to a request only the device's main user can make (managing users, updates, restart, storage, Wi-Fi, the bridge, logs), sent by an additional user's account on the same device. An instance is one user's own copy of the device's software.

dev.err.unknown_request.text: This device does not understand that request: its software is older than the app. Check for updates in Settings.
dev.err.unknown_request.note: Error reply to a request the device's software doesn't know: the app is newer than the device. Settings is the app's Settings screen, where the device's Update button is.
